title: LinkedIn - Services, SLO & Business KPIs
description: Uptime, latency, errors, SLI/SLO, business KPIs, JVM, containers and nodes for every service.

options.content:
**Service SLOs** (30-day style targets evaluated over the selected time range):

* **Availability SLI** = requests that did *not* return 5xx / all requests. **SLO 99.5 %** -> error budget 0.5 %.
* **Latency SLI** = share of requests answered in < 500 ms. **SLO 95 %**.
* **Burn rate** = (observed error ratio) / (allowed error ratio). 1 = budget consumed exactly at the SLO pace; >1 burns faster (page at 14.4 over 1h).

Request metrics come from the OpenTelemetry Java agent (`http_server_request_duration_seconds_*`), business KPIs from the manual `Telemetry` classes, uptime from the collector's `httpcheck` probes. Related: [Kafka](/d/linkedin-kafka) · [MySQL](/d/linkedin-mysql) · [ProxySQL](/d/linkedin-proxysql) · [Redis](/d/linkedin-redis).

panels.description: 100 % = no 5xx; 0 % = the 0.5 % budget of the 99.5 % SLO is used up; negative = SLO breached.

panels.description: SLO: 95 % of requests under 500 ms.

panels.description: Error-budget burn rate over the last 5 minutes (1 = on budget).

panels.description: 401s issued by the API gateway.

panels.description: Probes every 15 s from the collector.

panels.description: httpcheck_duration is reported in ms.

panels.title: Process uptime
panels.description: Seconds since the JVM started; drops reveal restarts.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (service_name, http_route, le) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service_name=~"$service"}[15m]))))
